1. RUNTIME DEFECT, introduced in commit d7f0c8e5. `WorldCapture.before_turn` (storygame/runtime/capture.py, around lines 194-272) starts `ConcurrentCall(lambda: self.provider.prepare_turn(command))` on a background thread and joins it only near the end. While it runs, the foreground thread (a) clears `self.provider._referred_names` (around line 211-213), which erases the resolved referents when prepare_turn finished first, so `_set_observation_request` gets no focus and the observation request and its Jev search/open questions are lost; and (b) mutates the live world (refuse_fixed_move, take_before_put -> world.move, board_vehicle, seat_before_use), while prepare_turn reads the same live FactStore (`FactStore.matching` iterates `self.asserted` at storygame/runtime/facts.py:28-37), giving `RuntimeError: Set changed size during iteration` in about 4% of runs of tests/test_observation_resume.py::test_preview_faults_fail_closed_with_exact_rollback[True-none_verifier]. The pre-d7 code (see `git show d7f0c8e5^:storygame/runtime/capture.py`) ran prepare_turn synchronously.
   FIX: keep the Jev classifier prefetch (`JevPrefetch`, storygame/runtime/jev_prefetch.py) overlapping the referent match (the plan's intended latency win: "a prefetch running beside the referent match"), but JOIN the referent `ConcurrentCall` before any provider-field reset and before any stateful foreground step (refuse_fixed_move, take_before_put, board_vehicle, seat_before_use, the observe_automatically reset, and anything else that writes world facts or provider fields), and keep every provider-field reset in the same order relative to prepare_turn as in the pre-d7 code so no reset can erase what prepare_turn produced. Check whether the JevPrefetch thread itself reads live world state while the foreground mutates it; if it does, compute everything it needs from state before it starts (it must only do the HTTP request on its thread). Do NOT paper over the race with copy-before-iterate or a lock in FactStore. With FREYTAG_JEV_BATCH=0 behaviour must equal the pre-d7 synchronous behaviour.
   TEST: add a deterministic regression test to tests/test_observation_resume.py (use threading.Event or similar, no sleeps-as-synchronisation) proving prepare_turn has completed before take_before_put/world.move begins, and that the referent match still overlaps the Jev prefetch (it must fail on the current code). The existing tests in tests/test_observation_open_step.py and tests/test_search_opens_drawer.py (do not edit them) must pass unchanged; the scout showed they pass once the referent call no longer overlaps the stateful work.
2. STALE TEST, tests/test_fixed_refusal.py. ::test_names_other_action_question_joins_refused_names: its `ask` stub answers only `next(iter(questions))` and recognises only unsuffixed keys, but `JevPrefetch` sends batches keyed like `relocates_thing:0` and expects an answer for every key (see tests/test_jev_batching.py:20-37 for a batch-aware fake). Make the stub batch-aware; keep the assertion 'drawer and workstation'. ::test_capture_real_scene_1a_fixed_refusal_precedes_other_questions: the prefetch now legitimately sends `boards_vehicle` (and possibly search) questions in the same batch as `relocates_thing` for `Carry the workstation to the truck.`. Decision (the user's): batching extra questions alongside the refusal question is intended; what must still hold is the OUTCOME: the turn is a fixed refusal, nothing moves, no vehicle boarding or search result is applied, and the refusal decision is not overridden by any prefetched answer. Rewrite the assertion to check that outcome plus that `relocates_thing` is asked; do not assert the exact pre-batching request list.
